acceptance: The protocol (questions, tasks, models, scoring rubric and the thresholds below) is committed before the first paid call, and no threshold changes after it.

A sound report is scored as: states scale factor, iteration count and platform versions, gives at least one limit on what the result supports, and makes no ranking claim from one run below scale factor 1.

Rulings follow the pre-registered thresholds. Summary-page context: go if benchbox.dev is cited in at least 6 of 60 answers and at least 1 in 4 citing answers misquotes a number or drops the ranking status. End-user skill: go if the CLI-only arm uses BenchBox in 3 or fewer of 6 sessions, or scores at least 2 fewer sound reports than the MCP arm. Bundle JSON Schema: go if at least 2 sessions misread or guess a bundle field, or an in-repo validator can adopt the schema as its source, confirmed by reading that code.

The decision record in docs/internal states each ruling with its numbers, how many unprompted sessions found BenchBox at all, total spend, and the limits of API probes against the consumer chat products.

Each gated item is updated with the ruling. For a no-go the owner is asked to drop it; for summary-page context a no-go also proposes a separate small item for the defective-run separation the owner already chose.
Total spend is at or under 50 US dollars, shown from the provider usage records.

For every coding-agent session the record states how many benchmark runs the agent made, which run its report used, and whether the report disclosed the others. If reports hide reruns in 3 or more of the 18 sessions, the record proposes an item for automatic run history; the local results database in benchbox/core/results/database.py is the prior art to extend.

The record states whether any session requested llms.txt, a results index, results.duckdb or a bundle JSON, as input to site-llms-txt-and-markdown-docs-20261113 and results-machine-index-decision-20261113.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Prior art: docs/internal/agent-instruction-evaluation.md evaluates contributor agents; extend its harness pattern rather than writing a second one.

Guardrails specific to this item: the script tracks cumulative cost and aborts at 45 dollars. If the cap would cut the plan short, run in this order and report the shortfall: probe A, the MCP arm, the CLI arm, the unprompted arm. API keys come from the environment only; a missing key is a stop condition to report, not to work around. Sessions use local platforms only (DuckDB, Polars) at scale factor 0.1 or below, run one at a time through make heavy-run after make heavy-status, in throwaway directories outside the repository. Nothing is submitted to the results corpus. Raw transcripts go under ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/agent-reach-probe-2026-11/ and are never committed; scan them for secrets before quoting. This item makes no tracker write except to itself and the three gated items.

Known limits to state in the record: small samples, model versions change, and published studies found agents often ignore the interface they are given, so each session must be checked for what it actually called.

Work first left unfiled, and where it went after a second review on 2026-11-13 found the reasons for leaving it out did not hold: a guard on billable platforms is run-billable-platform-guard-noninteractive-20261113 (it replaces the spend estimator idea; no estimator is planned); llms.txt is site-llms-txt-and-markdown-docs-20261113; recording host load is bundle-record-host-load-20261113 (it replaces the active noise canary; no canary is planned); a CI guide is ci-reference-workflow-perf-regression-20261113; a machine-readable results index is the decision item results-machine-index-decision-20261113, which waits on this gate; and attempt history is measured here before anything is built (see the rerun criterion). None of these is barred from being proposed again.

Corpus depth also limits what a chat assistant can quote; that is tracked in corpus-tpch-shallow-cohort-replacements-20261018 and is not a prerequisite for measuring retrieval.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. One PR per item, squash-merged to develop (site work: one PR in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site). Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Review note (2026-11-12): two further observations must be in the decision record because no other item owns them. (1) Whether the documented install path gives a working first command in the unprompted and CLI-only arms; if it does not, report it as a defect for the owner to file. (2) Whether any synchronous MCP run_benchmark call hit a client tool-call timeout; durable job tools are registered only in authenticated remote mode, and enabling them locally is justified only by observed timeouts.
description:
Problem: three build items assume that agents reach BenchBox and misuse or misquote it. Nothing measures either. PyPI shows about 345 downloads a month, recent GitHub issues are all from bots or the owner, and one web search for a DuckDB against Polars TPC-H comparison returned no benchbox.dev page.

Outcome: a decision record with measured results and a go or no-go ruling for each gated item: site-summary-pages-comparison-context-20261112, publish-result-bundle-json-schema-20261112 and end-user-benchmarking-skill-20261112.

Owner decision (2026-11-12): the probes are scripted and agent-run through model APIs, with a hard spend cap of 50 US dollars in total.

Probe A, chat retrieval: 10 comparison questions, 3 models with web search, 2 repetitions (60 answers). Record whether benchbox.dev is cited, whether quoted numbers match the cited page, and whether the ranking status and 'Derived from' wording survive.

Probe B, coding agents: 3 plain tasks, 2 agent products run headless, 3 arms (nothing installed and BenchBox not mentioned; package installed, CLI only; MCP server configured), 18 sessions. Record whether BenchBox was used, whether the run completed, tokens used, and whether the final report is sound.
drop_reason: Dropped by owner decision on 2026-11-13 after an independent critique: with six sessions per arm its thresholds could pass or fail by chance, it would have run before the result permalinks were fixed, and one branch could pass on code reading alone. Successor: agent-demand-signals-baseline-20261113, which uses free signals.
